In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in alpha-N-acetygalactosaminidosis the residual alpha-N-acetyglactosaminidate activity is sufficient to degrade only the simplest glycolipids containing alpha-GalNAcbeta1-4Galbeta1-4Glc-Cer, but not more complex GSLs.

the deficiency of lysosomal alpha-n-acetylgalctosaminidase is responsible for the accumulation of glycolipid with terminal alpha-GALNAc residues in fibroblats of patients with infantile neuroaxional dystrophy.
in alpha-N-acetygalactosaminidasic deficient fibroblasts the degradation of glycolipid molecules with terminal alpha-GalnAc residues is severely impaired.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the deficiency of alpha-N-Ac-GalNAc in the lysosomal fraction of fibroblastic cells is reflected by an impairment of the degradation of all glycolipids tested, and that the residual activity of this enzyme in the patients' cells is sufficient to allow for some degradation of the substrates.

the deficiency of alpha-N-Ac-galactosaminase activity results in impaired degradation of Forssman and blood group B GSL in fibroblast homogenates, and that this deficiency is also expressed in intact fibroblasts.

the alpha-N-acetygalactosaminidases of fibroblastic cell homogenates from the two patients were deficient in activity, and that the residual activity was sufficient to account for the residual modification of the Forssman GL and the neoglycolipoprotein in intact cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deficiency of alpha-N-Acetyl-Galactosaminase activity can be detected by using a variety of glycolipid probes.
alpha-N-acetygalactosaminidases is an essential enzyme for the degradation of GSL containing alpha-GalNAcs in the terminal position.
alpha-N-acetygalactosaminidases are involved in the metabolism of a variety of glycolipid species and not only of gangliosides.
